bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42483053 (fmt): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 2 found by fuzz target fuzzer_named_arg [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42483053
bug_description.normalized: The fuzz target passes a named-argument name into `fmt::arg` as an arbitrary `basic_string_view`. `internal::init_named_args()` later stores only `arg.name.data()` in `named_arg_info.name`, discarding the explicit length. When the two-byte format string `"{k"` is parsed, `parse_arg_id()` emits the named id `"k"` before the missing-`}` error path, and named lookup compares that id against the stored raw pointer. The comparison implicitly constructs `basic_string_view(const char*)` from the one-byte non-NUL buffer, so `std::char_traits<char>::length` / `strlen` reads past the heap allocation and ASan reports a heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled bytes that later become the overread pointer.
source.value_from: The exact witness is `12 20 ff ff ff ff 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 7b 6b`. Byte 0 low nibble `0x2` selects `invoke_fmt<signed char>`, high nibble `0x1` makes `argsize == 1`, and after the fixed 16-byte payload byte 17 `0x20` is wrapped here as a length-1 name with no NUL terminator.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: Crash site. The implicit conversion from stored named-argument pointer to `basic_string_view` computes the length with `strlen` on the 1-byte non-NUL heap buffer.

root_cause.description: The named-argument table stores only `arg.name.data()`, dropping the explicit length carried by `basic_string_view` and leaving later lookup to treat the attacker-controlled name as a C string.

parser_admitted.description: At this call the witness-controlled format string and named argument are handed to fmt's formatting pipeline; the later parser and named-lookup frames in the sanitizer stack all execute from this submission point.

tainted_value_origin.description: The sized name view that is later downgraded to a raw pointer for lookup.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: With `FMT_FUZZ_SEPARATE_ALLOCATION` enabled, lines 32-33 allocate exactly one heap byte for `argnamebuffer` and copy the single byte `0x20` into it before this line wraps it as a length-1 `fmt::string_view`.
tainted_value_origin.note: The ASan allocation stack points back to `std::vector<char> argnamebuffer(argsize);` at line 32, confirming the backing region is exactly one byte.

fine_trace.note: For this witness, `argsize == 1` and the earlier guard `argsize <= 0 || argsize >= Size` is false after the fixed 16-byte payload, so execution reaches this block. It allocates a separate 1-byte heap buffer, copies byte 17 `0x20` into it, wraps it as a length-1 `fmt::string_view`, and advances the cursor to the remaining bytes.
The remaining two bytes `0x7b 0x6b` become the exact format string `"{k"` in a separate buffer. That is the only format text seen by fmt on the crashing path.

fine_trace.code:
named_arg(basic_string_view<Char> name, const T& val)
    : named_arg_base<Char>(name), value(val) {}
fine_trace.note: The call `fmt::arg(argname, item1)` constructs a named argument whose `name` member keeps the sized `basic_string_view` from step 1. No NUL terminator is required yet because the name is still represented as pointer plus explicit length 1.

When `format_to` packs the argument store, this helper serializes the named-argument table using only `arg.name.data()`. The step discards the length preserved in step 3 and leaves `named_arg_info.name` as a raw pointer to the 1-byte buffer.

Parsing the format string from step 2 reaches the name branch at `'k'`, advances `it` to the end of `"{k"`, and emits the named id `"k"` as a length-1 `basic_string_view`. The missing closing brace is checked only after this handler call, so named lookup runs first.

Named lookup receives the parsed id `k` from step 5 and iterates the serialized table from step 4. The comparison uses the stored raw pointer `named_args.data[i].name` on the left and the parsed `basic_string_view` on the right.

The comparison in step 6 implicitly converts the left-hand `const char*` into `basic_string_view`, so this constructor calls `std::char_traits<char>::length(s)` / `strlen` on the raw pointer from step 4. That pointer still names the 1-byte allocation from step 1, which has no in-bounds NUL terminator, so ASan reports a 2-byte heap-buffer-overflow read at `0x602000000091`.

crash_stack.function: void invoke_fmt<signed char>(unsigned char const*, unsigned long, unsigned int)

allocation_stack.function: void invoke_fmt<signed char>(unsigned char const*, unsigned long, unsigned int)

format.name: libFuzzer raw byte stream
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact 20-byte witness staged in `poc`: `12 20 ff ff ff ff 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 7b 6b`. Byte 0 low nibble `0x2` selects `invoke_fmt<signed char>`, and high nibble `0x1` makes `argsize == 1`. `invoke_fmt` then treats bytes 1-16 as the fixed-width item payload and padding, byte 17 `0x20` as the entire named-argument buffer, and bytes 18-19 `7b 6b` as format string `"{k"`. Because `FMT_FUZZ_SEPARATE_ALLOCATION` is enabled, that name lives in its own 1-byte heap allocation with no terminator. This exact layout is sufficient: `fmt::arg` accepts the sized name, `init_named_args()` stores only `arg.name.data()`, and parsing `"{k"` emits the named id `k` before the missing-`}` error path, so lookup converts the raw pointer back to `basic_string_view(const char*)` and `strlen` overreads the 1-byte allocation.
